title: Azure Monitor Alert State Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.24 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.24 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" operationName.value="Microsoft.Insights/activityLogAlerts/Activated/Action"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.24_azure_monitor_alert_stat_24"
| sort -_time
description: Alert state changes (fired, resolved) provide consolidated view of metric/log conditions. Centralizing in Splunk enables correlation.
value: Detecting azure monitor alert state changes early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.

knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Action Group to send alert payload to Splunk (Logic App or webhook). Ingest fired and resolved events. Dashboard active alerts by severity and resource group.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" operationName.value="Microsoft.Insights/activityLogAlerts/Activated/Action"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.24_azure_monitor_alert_stat_24"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect azure monitor alert state changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_24_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (alert, state, time), Timeline (alert history), Single value (active alerts)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure monitor alert state changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
